clues: I am part of the skeleton that carries your weight.
I am a long bone, and you have two of me.
I sit between a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below.
My neck often breaks when an older person falls on their hip.
I am the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
fact: The femoral neck fracture after a fall is a classic injury in older people with osteoporosis.

clues: I am small, and you can hardly see me from the outside.
I live in a group of eight close neighbours.
I sit on the thumb side, in the row closest to the forearm.
Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall makes doctors worry about me.
My blood comes in from the far end, so a fracture through my waist can leave my near pole to die.
fact: Scaphoid fractures may not show on the first X-ray, and poor blood supply puts the proximal pole at risk of avascular necrosis.

clues: You can feel me easily under your skin.
I am a long bone, but I lie flat instead of standing up.
I join your arm to the trunk, the only bony link between them.
I am the first bone to start hardening in the fetus.
I am the bone most often broken at birth and in falls on an outstretched hand, usually in my middle third.
fact: It is the only long bone that ossifies in membrane, and it is the most commonly fractured bone.

clues: I am a small bone in the neck.
I am shaped like a horseshoe.
I hold up the tongue and give muscles of swallowing a place to attach.
I touch no other bone at all.
When I am broken, forensic doctors start to think about strangulation.
fact: It is the only bone in the body that does not articulate with another bone.

clues: I am a bone you can move with your fingers.
I sit at the front of a large joint.
I am the biggest sesamoid bone, buried inside a tendon.
I make the quadriceps a stronger lever when you straighten your leg.
I usually slip out of place to the lateral side.
fact: The largest sesamoid bone sits in the quadriceps tendon and improves the leverage of knee extension.

clues: I carry messages to and from the lower limb.
I come from the lumbar and sacral roots.
I leave the pelvis through a large notch in the hip bone, usually below the piriformis.
A badly placed injection in the upper outer buttock is safe, but the lower inner part can hurt me.
I am the thickest and longest nerve in the body, splitting into tibial and common fibular branches.
fact: It is the largest nerve in the body; gluteal injections go in the upper outer quadrant to avoid it.

clues: I am a nerve that works every few seconds, day and night.
I come from the neck, from roots C3, C4 and C5.
I run down over the scalenus anterior muscle and then through the chest beside the heart.
Pain from my territory can be felt at the tip of the shoulder.
I am the only motor supply to the diaphragm.
fact: "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive": damage paralyses half of the diaphragm.

clues: I am a branch of a cranial nerve.
I take a long trip down into the chest and then climb back up.
On the left I hook under the aortic arch; on the right, under the subclavian artery.
Surgeons look for me carefully during thyroid operations.
If I am cut on one side, the voice becomes hoarse.
fact: It supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid, so injury causes hoarseness.

clues: I come from the brachial plexus.
I run down the middle of the arm, beside the brachial artery.
I pass through a tight tunnel at the wrist under the flexor retinaculum.
When I am squeezed there, the thumb, index and middle fingers tingle at night.
I am the nerve trapped in carpal tunnel syndrome, and damage can waste the thenar muscles.
fact: Compression in the carpal tunnel gives numbness of the lateral three and a half fingers and thenar wasting.

clues: I come from the medial cord of the brachial plexus.
I supply most of the small muscles of the hand.
I run behind the medial epicondyle, where you can roll me under your finger.
When you knock me there, your little finger tingles.
People call me the funny bone, and my injury leaves a claw hand.
fact: Injury causes a claw hand with loss of finger abduction and numbness of the little finger.
decoys: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm

clues: I am a branch in the lower limb.
I split off from a much bigger nerve above the knee.
I wrap around the neck of the thin outer leg bone, right under the skin.
A tight plaster cast or crossing your legs for too long can press on me.
When I am damaged, the foot drops and the toes drag when you walk.
fact: It is the most commonly injured nerve in the leg, causing foot drop.

clues: I am one of twelve paired nerves that leave the brain.
I travel through a narrow bony canal in the temporal bone.
I carry taste from the front two thirds of the tongue and make tears and saliva flow.
I leave the skull through the stylomastoid foramen and pass through the parotid gland.
When I fail on one side, the whole half of the face droops, as in Bell palsy.
fact: Bell palsy is an idiopathic lower motor neuron lesion that paralyses one whole side of the face.

clues: I am a cranial nerve.
My name means "wanderer", because I travel far from the head.
I reach the heart, lungs and gut down to the last part of the transverse colon.
Pressing on the carotid sinus can make me slow the heart down.
I am the main parasympathetic nerve of the body, number ten of twelve.
fact: It carries most of the body's parasympathetic supply to the thoracic and abdominal organs.

clues: I am a muscle you use without thinking.
I am shaped like a dome.
I separate two big body cavities.
The aorta, oesophagus and inferior vena cava pass through me at different levels.
I am the main muscle of breathing: when I contract I flatten and pull air in.
fact: The vena cava passes at T8, the oesophagus at T10 and the aorta at T12.

clues: I am a muscle of the upper limb.
I give the shoulder its round shape.
My shape looks like an upside-down triangle, like a Greek letter.
The axillary nerve supplies me, and nurses often give vaccines into me.
I lift the arm away from the side, from about 15 to 90 degrees.
fact: Supplied by the axillary nerve, it is the main abductor of the arm and a common injection site.

clues: I am a muscle of the neck.
I divide the neck into front and back triangles.
I run from the breastbone and collarbone up to the bony bump behind the ear.
When I am tight in a newborn, the head tilts to one side.
I turn the face to the opposite side, and the accessory nerve supplies me.
fact: Torticollis in babies is often from a shortened muscle; contraction turns the head to the opposite side.

clues: I am a muscle on the side of the chest.
My edge has a jagged, saw-like look.
I hold the shoulder blade flat against the rib cage.
The long thoracic nerve supplies me and can be cut in breast surgery.
When I am paralysed, the shoulder blade sticks out like a wing.
fact: Long thoracic nerve injury paralyses it and causes a winged scapula.

clues: I am a muscle you cannot feel from the outside.
I start on the sides of the lumbar spine.
I join another muscle and attach to the lesser trochanter.
An abscess from spinal tuberculosis can track down inside my sheath into the groin.
I am the strongest flexor of the hip.
fact: Together with iliacus it forms iliopsoas, the main hip flexor; a sign of irritation is pain on hip extension.

clues: I am a muscle of the buttock.
I am fan-shaped and lie partly under a bigger muscle.
My nerve leaves the pelvis above the piriformis.
I keep the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.
When I am weak, the pelvis drops on the opposite side as you walk: the Trendelenburg sign.
fact: Weakness gives a positive Trendelenburg sign and a waddling gait.

clues: I am a small muscle at the back of a joint.
I lie deep, on the floor of a diamond-shaped fossa.
Part of me attaches to the lateral meniscus.
I am supplied by the tibial nerve.
I unlock the fully straightened knee by rotating it at the start of bending.
fact: It is called the key that unlocks the knee.

clues: I am a blood vessel.
I come from a short trunk that leaves the aorta.
I run down the groove between the two ventricles on the front of the heart.
I supply the front two thirds of the septum and much of the left ventricle.
When I block suddenly, the heart attack is so deadly I am called the widow maker.
fact: It is the most commonly blocked coronary artery and gives anterior myocardial infarctions.

clues: I am a branch of the maxillary artery.
I enter the skull through the foramen spinosum.
I run on the inner surface of the skull, under the thin pterion.
A blow to the side of the head can tear me.
My bleeding gives an extradural haematoma with a lucid interval.
fact: Rupture under the pterion causes an extradural (epidural) haematoma with a lucid interval.

clues: I am a vein of the lower limb.
I am superficial, lying just under the skin.
I start in front of the medial malleolus at the ankle.
I join the deep system at the groin through an opening in the fascia.
Surgeons often take me to use as a bypass graft for the heart.
fact: The longest vein in the body, often harvested for coronary artery bypass grafts.

clues: I am a vein in the chest.
My name means "unpaired".
I drain the back of the chest wall on the right side.
I arch over the root of the right lung.
I join the superior vena cava and connect it with the inferior vena cava when it is blocked.
fact: It links the two venae cavae and becomes an important bypass route when one is obstructed.

clues: I am a blood vessel that does not go straight back to the heart.
I am made where two veins meet behind the neck of the pancreas.
I carry blood rich in nutrients from the gut.
When pressure in me rises, varices can open in the oesophagus.
I bring about three quarters of the liver's blood supply.
fact: Raised pressure (portal hypertension) causes oesophageal varices, ascites and splenomegaly.

clues: I am made of several blood vessels.
I sit at the base of the brain.
I join the internal carotid and the vertebrobasilar systems.
Berry aneurysms often form where my vessels meet.
I am a ring that can keep blood flowing to the brain if one feeding artery is blocked.
fact: Most berry aneurysms occur on it, especially at the anterior communicating artery.

clues: I am a vessel, but I don't carry blood.
I start in the abdomen as a sac called the cisterna chyli.
I climb through the chest beside the oesophagus.
I empty at the junction of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins.
I carry most of the body's lymph and the fat absorbed from the gut.
fact: Injury causes chylothorax, milky fluid in the pleural space.

clues: I am an organ in the abdomen.
I sit high on the left, under ribs 9 to 11.
I filter the blood and remove old red cells.
I am the organ most often damaged in blunt abdominal trauma.
Without me, people are at risk of serious infection by encapsulated bacteria.
fact: After its removal patients need vaccines against pneumococcus, meningococcus and Haemophilus.

clues: I am a small part of the digestive tract.
I am a narrow tube with a closed end.
I hang from the caecum, where the three taeniae coli meet.
My base lies at McBurney's point on the skin.
When I am inflamed, pain starts around the navel and moves to the right lower abdomen.
fact: Its base projects to McBurney's point, one third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

clues: I am an organ that lies behind the stomach.
I am both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.
My head sits in the curve of the duodenum and my tail reaches the spleen.
My main duct joins the common bile duct at the ampulla of Vater.
I make digestive enzymes and, in my islets, insulin and glucagon.
fact: A gallstone stuck at the ampulla is a common cause of acute inflammation of this organ.

clues: I am a gland in the neck.
I am shaped like a butterfly.
My two lobes are joined by an isthmus in front of the trachea.
I move up when you swallow, because I am wrapped to the larynx.
I make hormones that set your metabolic rate, and I need iodine to do it.
fact: Lack of iodine makes it enlarge into a goitre.

clues: I am a gland in the head.
I am about the size of a pea.
I sit in a saddle of bone called the sella turcica.
A tumour in me can press on the optic chiasm and cause bitemporal hemianopia.
People call me the master gland, as I control many other glands.
fact: Tumours press on the optic chiasm above it, causing loss of both outer visual fields.

clues: I am a passage, not an organ.
I am at the wrist.
My floor is made of small bones and my roof is the flexor retinaculum.
Nine tendons and one nerve pass through me.
When I get too tight, the median nerve is squeezed.
fact: It contains the median nerve and nine flexor tendons; compression causes carpal tunnel syndrome.

clues: I am a passage through the abdominal wall.
I am about four centimetres long and run obliquely.
I have a deep ring and a superficial ring.
In men I carry the spermatic cord; in women, the round ligament.
Indirect hernias come down through me.
fact: Indirect inguinal hernias pass through the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.

clues: I am a small hollow on the body surface.
You can see me best when you stretch your thumb back.
My borders are tendons of the thumb muscles.
The radial artery runs across my floor.
Pain here after a fall suggests a fracture of the scaphoid.
fact: Tenderness here after a fall on an outstretched hand points to a scaphoid fracture.

clues: I am a group, not a single structure.
I am made of four muscles and their tendons.
My members are supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis.
I hold the head of the humerus in its shallow socket.
My supraspinatus part tears most often, giving a painful arc.
fact: The four "SITS" muscles stabilise the shoulder joint.

clues: I am a strong band inside a joint.
I cross another band of my own kind.
I run from the front of the tibia to the back of the femur.
I stop the tibia from sliding forward.
I tear in sudden twisting injuries in football, and the anterior drawer test checks me.
fact: Tears are common in pivoting sports; the Lachman and anterior drawer tests examine it.

clues: I am a strong cord at the back of the leg.
I join muscles to bone.
I am made by the gastrocnemius and soleus joining together.
I attach to the heel bone.
I am the thickest and strongest tendon in the body, and squeezing the calf tests if I am torn.
fact: The Thompson (calf squeeze) test checks for its rupture.

clues: I am a passage in the head.
I connect two spaces filled with air.
I run from the middle ear to the nasopharynx.
In children I am shorter and more horizontal, so infections climb up easily.
I open when you swallow or yawn to even out the pressure on the eardrum.
fact: It equalises middle ear pressure, which is why swallowing helps on a plane.

clues: I am part of the brain.
I am made of white matter.
I lie deep in the middle, under the longitudinal fissure.
If I am cut, the two sides of the brain can no longer share information.
I am the largest bundle of fibres joining the two cerebral hemispheres.
fact: It is the largest commissure, connecting the left and right hemispheres.

clues: I am a small group of special cells.
I am found in the wall of the heart.
I sit in the right atrium, near where the superior vena cava enters.
My cells leak sodium slowly, so they fire on their own without any nerve.
I am the natural pacemaker that sets the normal heart rate.
fact: Its cells have the fastest spontaneous depolarisation, so they set the sinus rhythm.

clues: I am a small cluster of special heart cells.
I sit in the floor of the right atrium, near the opening of the coronary sinus.
I am the only normal electrical path from the atria to the ventricles.
I slow the signal down on purpose, which shows as the PR interval.
That pause lets the atria finish filling the ventricles before they contract.
fact: Its delay (most of the PR interval) gives the atria time to empty into the ventricles.

clues: I am a network inside the heart.
I am made of large, pale muscle cells full of glycogen.
I spread under the inner lining of both ventricles.
I am the last part of the conduction system after the bundle branches.
I carry the impulse faster than any other heart tissue, so the ventricles contract together.
fact: They conduct at about 4 m/s, the fastest in the heart, for a coordinated ventricular contraction.

clues: I am a sensor in the neck.
I am a small widening at the start of an artery.
My nerve endings feel stretch and report through the glossopharyngeal nerve.
When blood pressure rises, I tell the brain to slow the heart.
Massaging me can stop some fast heart rhythms, but it can make older people faint.
fact: Carotid sinus massage raises vagal tone and can end supraventricular tachycardia.

clues: I am a tiny organ in the neck.
I sit at the fork where the main artery of the neck splits in two.
I have one of the highest blood flows per gram of any tissue.
My type I cells sense the blood's gases and acidity.
I raise breathing when the oxygen pressure in arterial blood falls.
fact: It is the main peripheral sensor of low arterial oxygen.

clues: I am a substance, not a cell.
I am mostly made of phospholipids, especially dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine.
I line the inside of the alveoli as a thin film.
I lower surface tension so small air sacs don't collapse when you breathe out.
Babies born too early lack me and develop respiratory distress syndrome.
fact: Made by type II pneumocytes from about 24 to 28 weeks; steroids before preterm birth increase it.

clues: I am a protein found in huge numbers in your blood.
I am made of four chains, each holding a heme group.
My curve with oxygen is S-shaped because my parts help each other bind.
Carbon monoxide sticks to me about 200 times more tightly than oxygen does.
I live inside red blood cells and carry oxygen to the tissues.
fact: Its sigmoid oxygen curve comes from cooperative binding; 2,3-BPG shifts it to the right.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a glycoprotein.
Most of me is made by cells around the tubules of the kidney.
Low oxygen in the blood makes my level go up.
I tell the bone marrow to make more red blood cells.
fact: Kidney failure lowers it and causes anaemia; some athletes have abused it for doping.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a steroid made from cholesterol.
I come from the outer layer of the adrenal cortex, the zona glomerulosa.
Angiotensin II and high potassium make me rise.
I make the kidney keep sodium and lose potassium.
fact: An adrenal tumour making too much of it (Conn syndrome) causes high blood pressure with low potassium.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am made in the hypothalamus and stored in the posterior pituitary.
I rise when the blood gets too concentrated.
I put water channels, aquaporin-2, into the collecting ducts.
Without me you pass large amounts of dilute urine, as in diabetes insipidus.
fact: Lack of it causes central diabetes insipidus; alcohol blocks its release.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a small peptide.
I am released when the walls of the heart's upper chambers are stretched.
I make the kidney lose more salt and water and I widen blood vessels.
I am the heart's own hormone that works against the renin-angiotensin system.
fact: Released by atrial stretch, it promotes sodium excretion; its cousin BNP helps diagnose heart failure.

clues: I am a protein that cuts another protein.
I am made by special cells in the wall of the afferent arteriole.
Low pressure in the kidney, low sodium and sympathetic signals all make me rise.
I cut angiotensinogen from the liver into angiotensin I.
I am the first and rate-limiting step of the system that raises blood pressure.
fact: It starts the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system; aliskiren blocks it directly.

clues: I am a group of cells in the nephron.
My cells are tall and packed close together.
I sit in the wall of the distal tubule where it touches its own glomerulus.
I sense how much sodium chloride is flowing past me.
I send signals that adjust filtration and renin release: tubuloglomerular feedback.
fact: It senses NaCl in the distal tubule and controls GFR by tubuloglomerular feedback.

clues: I am part of the nephron.
I am shaped like a hairpin.
I dip down into the medulla and come back up.
My thick ascending limb pumps salt out but lets no water follow.
I build the salt gradient that lets the kidney make concentrated urine.
fact: Its countercurrent multiplier builds the medullary gradient; loop diuretics act on its thick ascending limb.

clues: I am a ball of very small blood vessels.
I sit between two arterioles, not between an artery and a vein.
Bowman's capsule wraps around me.
My wall has three layers that block cells and most proteins.
I am the filter of the nephron, where blood plasma becomes the first urine.
fact: Its filtration rate (GFR) is the main measure of kidney function.

clues: I am a group of cells in the kidney.
I am smooth muscle cells that have changed their job.
I sit in the wall of the afferent arteriole.
I hold granules and act as a pressure sensor.
I release renin when blood pressure in the kidney falls.
fact: Modified smooth muscle cells that release renin; with the macula densa they form an apparatus.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a steroid, and I am highest in the morning.
I come from the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex.
I raise blood sugar, break down protein and calm the immune system.
I am the body's main stress hormone, and ACTH controls me.
fact: Too much gives Cushing syndrome; too little gives Addison disease.

clues: I am a hormone.
I carry four iodine atoms.
Most of me travels in the blood bound to proteins.
Tissues change me into a more active form by removing one iodine.
I am the main hormone the thyroid gland releases.
fact: It is converted in the tissues to the more active T3.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a peptide made by four tiny glands in the neck.
Low calcium in the blood makes me rise.
I free calcium from bone, keep it in the kidney and lose phosphate in the urine.
I turn on the enzyme that makes active vitamin D.
fact: High levels from an adenoma cause high calcium: "bones, stones, groans and moans".

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a peptide made in the neck.
I come from the parafollicular C cells of the thyroid.
I lower blood calcium by slowing down osteoclasts.
I am a tumour marker for medullary thyroid cancer.
fact: It is raised in medullary thyroid carcinoma.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.
I am a small peptide of nine amino acids.
A baby sucking at the breast makes me rise and the milk flow out.
I make the womb contract during labour, and I am given as a drip to speed it up.
fact: It causes uterine contraction and milk let-down; it is used to induce labour.

clues: I am a hormone.
I come from the anterior pituitary.
Dopamine from the hypothalamus keeps me down all the time.
A tumour making too much of me can stop periods and cause milk outside pregnancy.
My main job is to make the breasts produce milk.
fact: Prolactinoma is the most common pituitary tumour; dopamine agonists treat it.

clues: I am a hormone.
I come from the anterior pituitary, mostly during deep sleep.
I work through IGF-1 from the liver.
Too much of me after the long bones stop lengthening causes acromegaly.
Too much of me in childhood makes a person very tall: gigantism.
fact: Excess before puberty causes gigantism; after it, acromegaly.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am made from serotonin.
I come from the pineal gland.
Light at the eyes stops my release.
I rise in the dark and help set the sleep-wake cycle.
fact: Sometimes taken to help with jet lag.

clues: I am a hormone of the gut.
I am made by G cells in the antrum of the stomach.
Protein in the stomach and stretching of its wall make me rise.
A tumour in the pancreas making too much of me gives many ulcers.
My main job is to make parietal cells release acid.
fact: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is a tumour that makes too much of it.

clues: I am a hormone of the gut.
I am made by I cells in the duodenum and jejunum.
Fat and protein reaching the small intestine make me rise.
I relax the sphincter of Oddi and help you feel full.
I make the gallbladder contract and the pancreas release enzymes.
fact: It squeezes the gallbladder, so a fatty meal can trigger biliary colic.

clues: I am a hormone, and the very first one ever discovered.
I am made by S cells in the duodenum.
Acid arriving from the stomach makes me rise.
I make the pancreas release water and bicarbonate.
I neutralise the acid entering the small intestine.
fact: The first hormone discovered (1902); it makes the pancreas secrete bicarbonate.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am made mainly by the stomach.
I rise before meals and fall after you eat.
I also make the pituitary release growth hormone.
People call me the hunger hormone.
fact: The only known gut hormone that increases appetite.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am made by fat cells.
The more body fat you have, the more of me there is.
I act on the hypothalamus.
I tell the brain that the body has enough energy stores, so appetite falls.
fact: Obese people usually have high levels but respond poorly to it (resistance).

clues: I am a protein, not a hormone.
I am made by the parietal cells of the stomach.
I bind a vitamin and protect it on its trip through the gut.
I am absorbed together with that vitamin in the terminal ileum.
Antibodies against me cause pernicious anaemia.
fact: It is needed to absorb vitamin B12; autoimmune loss causes pernicious anaemia.

clues: I am a group of molecules.
I am made by the liver from cholesterol.
I am stored in the gallbladder.
About 95% of me is taken back in the terminal ileum and reused.
I break fat into small drops so it can be digested and absorbed.
fact: They emulsify fat; their enterohepatic circulation recycles them several times a day.

clues: I am a sensor.
I lie inside a skeletal muscle, parallel to its fibres.
My special intrafusal fibres are supplied by gamma motor neurons.
I sense how much and how fast a muscle is stretched.
I start the knee-jerk reflex when the patellar tendon is tapped.
fact: It drives the stretch (myotatic) reflex such as the knee jerk.

clues: I am a sensor.
I sit where a muscle joins its tendon.
I lie in series with the muscle fibres.
My signals come through Ib fibres.
I sense tension and make the muscle relax if it pulls too hard.
fact: It mediates the inverse stretch reflex that protects against too much force.

clues: I am a sensor in the skin and deeper tissues.
I look like a sliced onion under the microscope.
I adapt very fast.
I am the biggest of the skin's touch sensors.
I sense vibration and deep pressure.
fact: Its onion-like layers make it respond to vibration and quickly adapt.

clues: I am part of the brain.
I sit below the thalamus and above the pituitary.
I control body temperature, hunger and thirst.
I make releasing hormones that reach the pituitary through portal vessels.
I am the link between the nervous system and the endocrine system.
fact: It controls the pituitary and keeps homeostasis (temperature, thirst, hunger).

clues: I am part of the brain.
I sit at the back of the skull, behind the brainstem.
I hold more neurons than the rest of the brain together.
Damage to me causes a wide-based gait, intention tremor and slurred speech.
I coordinate movement and balance.
fact: Damage gives ataxia on the same side, intention tremor and dysdiadochokinesia.

clues: I am a messenger between cells.
I am made from choline and a two-carbon unit carried by coenzyme A.
I am broken down in the gap by an esterase within milliseconds.
I act on nicotinic and muscarinic receptors.
I am released at the neuromuscular junction to make skeletal muscle contract.
fact: Myasthenia gravis is caused by antibodies against its nicotinic receptor.

clues: I am a messenger in the brain.
I am made from tyrosine.
I am the step just before noradrenaline.
Neurons making me in the substantia nigra die in Parkinson disease.
I am the brain's reward signal and I stop prolactin release.
fact: Loss in the nigrostriatal pathway causes Parkinson disease.

clues: I am a protein.
I hold iron in a heme group.
I have only one chain, so my curve with oxygen is not S-shaped.
When muscle is crushed, I leak out and can block the kidneys.
I store oxygen inside muscle cells.
fact: Released in rhabdomyolysis, it can cause acute kidney injury.

clues: I am a hormone.
I am a peptide made of two chains joined by disulfide bridges.
I come from the beta cells of the pancreatic islets, cut from a longer precursor with C-peptide.
I put GLUT4 transporters into the membranes of muscle and fat cells.
I am the only hormone that lowers blood sugar.
fact: Lack of it causes type 1 diabetes; C-peptide shows how much the body makes itself.

clues: I am an enzyme.
I add a phosphate to a sugar as soon as it enters the cell.
I work in the liver and in the beta cells of the pancreas.
Unlike my cousins, glucose-6-phosphate does not stop me, and I need a lot of sugar before I work fast.
I am the glucose sensor of the beta cell; faults in me cause a mild inherited diabetes, MODY 2.
fact: Its high Km makes it a glucose sensor; mutations cause MODY type 2.

clues: I am an enzyme.
I work in the cytoplasm.
I use ATP to add a second phosphate to a six-carbon sugar.
AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate switch me on; ATP and citrate slow me down.
I am the main control step of glycolysis.
fact: It catalyses the rate-limiting, committed step of glycolysis.

clues: I am an enzyme.
I work at the very end of a pathway in the cytoplasm.
I move a phosphate onto ADP and make ATP directly.
Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate switches me on ahead of time.
When I am missing in red cells, they cannot make enough energy and break down: a hemolytic anaemia.
fact: Its deficiency is the most common glycolysis enzyme defect that causes haemolytic anaemia.

clues: I am a group of enzymes working as one.
I live in the mitochondrial matrix.
I need five helpers: thiamine, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD and NAD.
Arsenic blocks me, and lack of vitamin B1 slows me down.
I turn pyruvate into acetyl-CoA, linking glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.

clues: I am an enzyme.

clues: I am an enzyme.

clues: I am a small peptide of three amino acids.

clues: I am an enzyme.

clues: I am a tissue.
I have many nuclei but no cell walls between them.
I invade the wall of the uterus.
I make hCG.
I am the outer layer of the placenta that talks to the mother's blood.
fact: Makes hCG, the hormone detected in pregnancy tests.

clues: I am a group of cells.
I am in the blastocyst.
I sit at one side of the cavity.
My cells are pluripotent stem cells.
I become the embryo itself.
fact: Gives rise to the embryo; source of embryonic stem cells.

clues: I am a sac.
I am found in the early embryo.
I make the first blood cells.
The primordial germ cells start in my wall.
Part of me becomes the gut, and I shrink later.
fact: The first site of blood formation.

clues: I am a small pouch.
I grow from the yolk sac into the stalk.
My vessels become the umbilical vessels.
Part of me becomes the urachus.
I join the bladder to the umbilicus.
fact: Becomes the urachus, which closes to the median umbilical ligament.

clues: I am a membrane.
I surround the embryo.
I am filled with fluid.
I protect the fetus from knocks.
I break when the waters break.
fact: Forms the amniotic sac.

clues: I am a membrane.
I am the outer membrane around the embryo.
I have villi.
My smooth part fades away.
My villous part helps form the placenta.
fact: The fetal part of the placenta.

clues: I am an opening in the heart.
I am between the atria.
I let blood skip the lungs before birth.
I usually close after the first breath.
If I stay open, a clot can cross to the brain.
fact: A patent foramen ovale can let clots pass (paradoxical embolism).

clues: I am a blood vessel.
I join the pulmonary artery to the aorta.
I let blood skip the lungs before birth.
Prostaglandin E keeps me open.
I close after birth, and indomethacin helps close me.
fact: Becomes the ligamentum arteriosum; a patent one makes a machinery murmur.

clues: I am a blood vessel.
I am in the fetal liver.
I carry oxygen-rich blood past the liver.
I close after birth.
I become the ligamentum venosum.
fact: Shunts placental blood past the liver to the inferior vena cava.

clues: I am a blood vessel.
I run in the cord between mother and baby.
I am alone; my two partners are arteries.
I carry the most oxygen-rich blood in the fetus.
I become the round ligament of the liver.
fact: Carries oxygenated blood from the placenta; becomes the ligamentum teres.

clues: I am part of the early heart tube.
I sit between the primitive ventricle and the truncus arteriosus.
Before the heart folds, I am one of its five swellings.
I make the smooth outflow parts of both ventricles.
I become the conus arteriosus of the right ventricle and the aortic vestibule of the left.
fact: Becomes the conus arteriosus and aortic vestibule.

clues: I am part of the early heart.
I am the outflow tract.
A spiral septum divides me.
If I don't divide, one big vessel leaves both ventricles.
I become the aorta and the pulmonary trunk.
fact: Splits into the aorta and pulmonary trunk; persistence is a cyanotic heart defect.

clues: I am part of the early heart.
I receive blood from veins.
My right horn joins the right atrium.
I form the smooth part of the right atrium.
My left horn becomes the coronary sinus.
fact: Becomes the smooth right atrium and the coronary sinus.

clues: I am a pouch in the neck.
I am lined by endoderm.
I make two organs.
I make the inferior parathyroids.
I make the thymus.
fact: Forms the thymus and inferior parathyroid glands.

clues: I am an arch in the neck.
I have the trigeminal nerve.
I make the muscles of chewing.
I make the malleus and incus.
I make the jaw.
fact: Gives rise to the jaw, malleus and incus.

clues: I am an arch in the neck.
I have the facial nerve.
I make the stapes.
I make the muscles of facial expression.
I make part of the hyoid.
fact: Gives rise to the stapes and muscles of facial expression.

clues: I am a duct.
I start at the foramen caecum of the tongue.
I go down the neck.
I usually disappear.
If I leave a cyst, it moves up when you stick out your tongue.
fact: A remnant forms a midline neck cyst that moves with tongue protrusion.

clues: I am a pouch.
I grow up from the roof of the mouth.
I meet a downgrowth of the brain.
I make the anterior pituitary.
My remains can form a craniopharyngioma.
fact: Becomes the anterior pituitary; leftovers can form craniopharyngioma.

clues: I am a duct.
I run beside the early kidney.
Testosterone keeps me alive.
I become the epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicles.
I make the male internal genital ducts.
fact: Forms male ducts under the influence of testosterone.

clues: I am a duct.
I run beside another duct.
Anti-Müllerian hormone makes me disappear in males.
I make the fallopian tubes and uterus.
I make the female internal genital tract.
fact: Forms the uterus, tubes and upper vagina.

clues: I am a bud.
I grow from the mesonephric duct.
I grow into the metanephric tissue.
I make the ureter, pelvis and collecting ducts.
I make the drainage part of the kidney.
fact: Forms the collecting system of the kidney.

clues: I am a tissue.
I am in the early kidney.
The ureteric bud talks to me.
I make the nephrons.
I make the filtering part of the kidney.
fact: Forms the nephrons, from glomerulus to distal tubule.

clues: I am a structure.
I join the bladder to the umbilicus.
I am a remains of the allantois.
I usually close.
If I stay open, urine leaks from the umbilicus.
fact: A patent one leaks urine from the umbilicus.

clues: I am a duct.
I join the gut to the yolk sac.
I usually close.
If I stay partly open, I leave a pouch in the ileum.
I can leave a Meckel diverticulum.
fact: Its remnant is Meckel's diverticulum.

clues: I am part of the early gut.
I am supplied by the superior mesenteric artery.
I turn 270 degrees around this artery.
I herniate into the umbilical cord.
If I turn wrongly, I can twist.
fact: Malrotation can lead to volvulus.

clues: I am a plate of mesoderm.
I am in the early embryo.
I sit between the heart and the yolk stalk.
I help make the liver.
I make the central tendon of the diaphragm.
fact: Forms the central tendon of the diaphragm.

clues: I am a pouch.
I go down to the scrotum.
I go with the testis.
I usually close.
If I stay open, an indirect hernia or hydrocele can form.
fact: A patent one leads to indirect inguinal hernia or hydrocele.

clues: I am a band.
I join the testis to the scrotum.
I guide the testis down.
In adult males my remnant is the scrotal ligament.
In females I become the round ligament.
fact: Guides the descent of the testis.

clues: I am a structure.
I am in the early embryo.
DHT makes me grow.
I become the penis in males.
I become the clitoris in females.
fact: Becomes the glans penis or clitoris.

clues: I am a structure.
I am part of the cloaca.
I make the bladder.
I make the urethra.
I make the prostate in males.
fact: Forms the bladder, urethra and prostate.

clues: I am a structure.
I am at the end of the hindgut.
I am divided by the urorectal septum.
I become the rectum and the urogenital sinus.
I am the common end of the gut and urinary tract.
fact: Divided by the urorectal septum into rectum and urogenital sinus.

clues: I am a ball of cells.
I have 16 cells.
I form about three days after fertilization.
I look like a mulberry.
I become the blastocyst.
fact: A solid ball of 16 cells that becomes the blastocyst.

clues: I am a ball of cells.
I have a fluid-filled cavity.
I form about five days after fertilization.
I have an inner cell mass and a trophoblast.
I implant in the uterus.
fact: Implants in the uterus at about day 6 to 7.

clues: I am a cell.
I am the first cell of a new life.
I have two sets of chromosomes.
I form when a sperm and an egg join.
I divide to make the embryo.
fact: Forms at fertilization.

clues: I am an organ.
I am made by both mother and fetus.
I make hormones.
I let oxygen and nutrients pass from the mother.
I am delivered after the baby, as the afterbirth.
fact: Exchanges gases and nutrients between mother and fetus.
